descriptionChirho: Not subject to decay, death, or corruption — imperishable, incorruptible, immortal. All three clusters represent the same adjective in different case/number/gender forms applied to things or persons that do not perish: the imperishable crown (1 Cor 9:25), the incorruptible God (Rom 1:23, 1 Tim 1:17), the imperishable inheritance (1 Pet 1:4,23), the incorruptible resurrection body (1 Cor 15:52). Spanish uses 'incorruptible/incorruptibles' throughout; Arabic 'غَيرِ فانٍ' / 'غَيْرَ فَانِيَ' / 'غَيرَ فاسِدينَ' (not perishing) and 'الَّذي لا يَفْنى' (who does not perish) — all negations of mortality; Korean '썩지 않는' (not rotting) uniformly; Swahili 'usioharibika/isiyoharibika/wasioharibika/asiyeharibika' are class-agreement variants of one adjective; Hindi 'अविनाशी' (avināśī = imperishable) consistently across all clusters.
